outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Foundations of LLM-Enhanced Tabular Learning
outline.description: In the realm of machine learning, traditional approaches to tabular data analysis often rely on models trained specifically on the statistical patterns found within a dataset. However, in real-world scenarios labeled with only a handful of examples—known as few-shot learning—these methods frequently falter due to overfitting or an inability to generalize. This limitation stems from the scarcity of data, which is a common bottleneck in industries such as healthcare and finance, where acquiring labeled records is prohibitively expensive. To bridge this gap, researchers have increasingly turned to Large Language Models (LLMs). These generalist models, trained on vast corpora of text, possess an immense reservoir of prior knowledge that can theoretically substitute for expert domain expertise.

outline.description: The paradigm shift offered by the \textsf{FeatLLM} framework represents a fundamental departure from conventional approaches to Large Language Models (LLMs) in tabular learning. Traditional methods, often referred to as end-to-end inference approaches, treat the LLM as a black-box classifier. In these standard pipelines, every single input sample is serialized into natural language and passed directly through the LLM, which processes the entire dataset for every prediction. This design suffers from significant computational overhead at inference time, as it requires repetitive LLM queries for each observation. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Prompt Engineering and Rule Extraction Strategies
outline.description: In the landscape of large language model (LLM) applications for tabular learning, the ability to reliably translate unstructured reasoning into structured data transformations is paramount. Conventional approaches often treat the LLM as a black-box predictor, feeding serialized table rows directly into the model to generate a probability distribution for the target class. However, this end-to-end black-box utilization incurs prohibitive computational costs at inference time and suffers from scalability issues when dealing with high-dimensional tabular data. To overcome these limitations, frameworks like \textsf{FeatLLM} reposition the LLM as an intelligent feature engineer. This chapter delves into the sophisticated prompt engineering techniques and structured reasoning strategies employed
